mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-27.7 to -25.3) as commuting and discretionary trips resume; because transit volume and retail footfall draw on the same trip-generation pool, continued transit recovery lifts RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean of -14.0 over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -27.7 to -25.3 across four weekly means
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above -14.0 even though TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM peaked at +3.3 and has unwound to +1.9, marking the end of household pantry stocking; the released grocery budget and time shift toward discretionary trips, so a crossing back below +2.0 predicts higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +2.0 after having peaked above +3.0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from +3.3 at t-1w to +1.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM crosses below +2.0 is lower than in the two weeks before the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Retail footfall is jointly gated by outdoor recreation and transit capacity; when PARKS holds above -12 while TRANSIT keeps recovering, mall-anchored discretionary trips rise multiplicatively rather than additively, so RETAIL_REC increases over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above -12 and TRANSIT above -26 simultaneously for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -18.4 to -10.0 while TRANSIT improved from -27.7 to -25.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in weeks when both PARKS > -12 and TRANSIT > -26 hold simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: Singapore's scheduled move to Phase 3 reopening at end-December raises group-size limits and mall capacity; this policy shock lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks independently of the current mobility level, because it relaxes the binding constraint on in-store browsing.
candidate_trigger: the Phase 3 reopening effective date falls inside the next 28-day window
evidence_refs: fact:decision point 2020-12-15 precedes the end-December Phase 3 reopening
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC in the 28 days after the Phase 3 effective date is not above the 28-day mean preceding that date.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has deteriorated in each of the last four weeks (-14.1 to -16.4), signalling falling office occupancy rather than recovery; fewer weekday commuters depresses lunchtime and after-work retail spend, pulling RETAIL_REC below its recent mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines in three or more of four consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -14.1 to -16.4 across four weekly means
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES keeps declining week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has stayed pinned between +13.4 and +14.1 for four consecutive weeks, indicating a durable home-centric routine; time and expenditure retained at home substitute for mall trips, so RETAIL_REC stays at or below its current level over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held between +13.4 and +14.1 for four weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the last-28-day mean of -14.0 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +13.

mechanism_narrative: Year-end festive shopping and the school holiday period create a calendar-locked demand pull that lifts RETAIL_REC within one week irrespective of mobility indices, because seasonal spending is driven by the date rather than by trip-supply conditions.
candidate_trigger: the forecast week contains the Christmas or New Year public holiday
evidence_refs: fact:decision point 2020-12-15 sits two weeks before New Year
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the week containing Christmas and New Year is not above the t-0w value of -13.7.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week TRANSIT path is decelerating (-27.7, -26.3, -25.7, -25.3 with shrinking weekly gains); if TRANSIT deteriorates by more than 2 points week-on-week, trip-capacity scarcity returns and RETAIL_REC falls within two weeks as discretionary trips are cancelled first.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 2.0 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly gains shrank from +1.4 to +0.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower two weeks after any week in which TRANSIT declines by more than 2.0 points.
